Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

SimSurvey 0.1.8.9000 (development)

  • Add fishery target modes for shares of Z, fully selected F (F_full), catch numbers (catch_n), and catch kilograms (catch_kg).

  • Validate starting-population limits, mortality-compatible targets and combined reference F before random stock allocation, with fishery/year/age diagnostics. Cap kilogram catches as whole-fish aggregate removals and record target units, requested settings, reference catches, achieved catches and shortfalls.

  • Update fishery plots and the workflow vignette for mixed target types, reference F and kilogram quotas, including the mathematical conversion.

  • Bound jointly rounded reference-number targets by the shared integer death count, preventing floating-point round trips at half-integer ties from creating an unsupported extra fish.

  • Check combined reference catches against N and B as well as Z, including length-selective fisheries whose biomass targets overlap on heavy fish.

  • Publish development documentation under /dev/, preserving the released site at the root. Build the site on pull requests before deployment from main. Use stable appendix anchors in both the vignette and website article.

  • Shorten the fisheries vignette, replace verification tables with explanations, and show a function-based workflow. Extend examples to ten years, improve imperfect harvester knowledge, and compare random with targeted fishing using series divided by their overall temporal means.

  • Specify the survey-map polygon trace type explicitly, removing Plotly’s inferred-scatter message without suppressing messages from plotting.

  • Base the new-workflow vignette on the documented five-age, 20-km survey example, with default biology, abundance, spatial processes, and survey allocation.

  • Replace the vignette’s fixed-core CPUE example with default shifting spatial distributions and imperfect current-year knowledge. Explain how changing concentration can steepen or flatten the CPUE-abundance relationship.

  • Clarify that fishery knowledge uses current-year density and fresh annual map errors, and verify that fishing locations follow a shifted population.

  • Use one controlled five-year population throughout the fisheries vignette, increase survey coverage to eight sets, match CPUE markers to their lines, and size widgets without deprecated Plotly layout arguments.

  • Increase spacing in fishery and survey map/composition graphics and keep zero-catch survey locations visible, including when marker counts are constant.

  • Prefer total_deaths in fishery reference diagnostics, clarifying that it is the shared age/year whole-fish total across fishing and other mortality. Retain death_budget as an identical compatibility alias.

  • Embed local widget support resources in the workflow vignette so its packaged HTML remains portable, while keeping one Plotly web bundle external and avoiding plotting-asset downloads during builds.

  • Revise the multi-fishery vignette around user-supplied allocations, explicit shortfalls/F diagnostics, survey catch kilograms, and package Plotly helpers. Add a controlled five-year preferential-fishing CPUE demonstration and its spatial-proportionality equations; separate backwards compatibility guidance.

  • Add Plotly fishery maps/compositions and annual trends with plot_fishery() and plot_fishery_trend(). Extend plot_trend(mat = ...) to biomass and mature biomass, with matching units and preserved positional calls.

  • Add deterministic individual survey catch weights and catch kilograms per set, age/set, and replicate/year, including batch, parallel, and scenario workflows. Weights use all caught fish, preserve RNG state, and remain missing when an older number-only simulation has no weight model.

  • Retain realized catches, removal fractions, and Baranov-equivalent F at age in fishery reference diagnostics, alongside original N, Z, and integer budgets. Clarify capture q units and the allocation/shortfall interpretation.

  • Correct fishery stock initialization to use only the current year’s spatial population. Previous multi-year fishery results pooled years and must be rerun from their saved populations; population trajectories need not be regenerated.

  • Expand “Simulating multiple fisheries and surveys” with default-based workflows, controlled targeting and monitoring comparisons, maturity observations, independent surveys, and a mathematical appendix explaining the extensions.

  • Add population-level weight and maturity relationships, sim_weight() and sim_maturity(), and a sim_growth() alias for sim_vonB(). Derive expected biomass (B, B_at_length) and mature biomass (S, S_at_length) from the joint length-age key; refresh mass summaries in spatial and rounded populations.

  • Move weight configuration from the unreleased fishery interfaces to sim_abundance(). Every fishery now shares the population weight relationship.

  • Prefer x50 to x0 in sim_logistic(), retaining positional calls and a deprecated named x0 alias without changing the default curve.

  • Add maturity_sampling = "aged", "measured", or "none" to fisheries and surveys, including batch, parallel, scenario, and resume workflows. Maturity observations and counts mask shared latent states after all existing sampling, preserving catches, reporting, existing samples and overlapping maturity states.

  • Add sim_fisheries(sim, ...) for interleaved fisheries sharing one stock and mortality budget, with joint target rounding and per-fishery effort/CPUE. Support unnamed mortality matrices returned by existing custom closures, while rejecting conflicting age/year labels.

  • Add sim_surveys(sim, ...) for independent programs observing one annual snapshot, and select_survey() for existing analyses and plots. Preserve the scenario-design table used by test_surveys(). Batch configurations are named and canonicalized; common replicate counts align across fisheries and surveys.

  • Add aggregate fishery simulation with explicit capture models, age/length gear selectivity, conditional mortality budgets, spatial depletion, effort and CPUE. Integrated reporting and nested biological sampling retain their inclusion probabilities and do not change fishing truth.

  • Add length-based survey catchability with q_by = "length", preserving the historical age-based default. Round and simulate on copies of caller tables.

  • Preserve dimensions in single-age length keys, spatial distributions, and rounded single-age or single-year populations.

  • Convert legacy inla.mesh inputs automatically for current INLA/fmesher in standard and barrier SPDE simulations, preserving the stored geometry and barrier triangle assignments. Use the current fmesher constructor in make_mesh() when available, avoiding INLA’s constructor deprecation warning.

  • Add repository guidance and an automated testthat suite covering the core population, spatial, survey, and analysis workflow, including parallel runs and export/resume. Archive the historical informal tests under analysis/.

  • Include tests in source-package checks and enable the existing CI matrix on the fisheries-0.2.0 development branch.

  • Reject descending, duplicated, empty, non-numeric, and non-finite age/year sequences in sim_abundance() with the documented sequence error.

  • Apply the current innovation scale throughout sim_ays_covar() when sd, phi_age, or phi_year varies. Cache only the spatial factor, and clarify that sd is a standard deviation rather than a variance.

  • Fix strat_means() for a single survey group, including replacement of undefined confidence-limit values with NA.

  • Allow group_lengths() to return an empty vector, so surveys with no catch or no measured lengths retain their set records without failing.

  • Preserve the retained survey’s I_at_length truth when running or resuming survey scenarios.

  • Explicitly assign the documented kilometre-based projected CRS in make_grid(); the data-frame conversion could leave the grid without a CRS.

SimSurvey 0.1.1

  • Initial release documented in Regular et al. (2020) <doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0232822>

SimSurvey 0.1.22020-09-09

  • Initial release to CRAN

SimSurvey 0.1.32021-01-13

  • Simplify make_grid function to improve the splits of the divisions and strata
  • CRAN request: change doi in DESCRIPTION to preferred format

SimSurvey 0.1.42022-01-26

  • Add a “bezier” method to make_grid
  • Allow a vector of age-specific parameters to be supplied to sim_parabola plus add some options for defining a more asymmetric parabola
  • Speed up sim_sets and ensure sample call passes new error traps
  • Fix bug in plotting scripts; plotly returns an error if supplied xtabs class data
  • Improve vis_fit function

SimSurvey 0.1.52022-04-06

  • Add informative error if NaN values are generated using sim_distribution
  • Fix showscale problem in sim_distribution; was supplying a logical vector when length should have been 1
  • Allow for more flexible simulation of sets by adding an argument to sim_sets called subset_cells and a custom_sets argument to sim_survey
  • Add number of fish available to the survey (I = N * q) to the sp_N object when running sim_survey

SimSurvey 0.1.62023-09-19

  • Switch to dependence on the sf and stars package rather than the sp and raster package given the evolution of R spatial
  • Switch to new INLAspacetime functions for simulating from a barrier mesh

SimSurvey 0.1.72025-08-22

  • Minor improvements to documentation
  • Dropped dependence on magrittr pipe (%>%); now using native R pipe (|>)

SimSurvey 0.1.82025-09-15

  • Add Matrix to Imports so lazy-loaded mesh data (survey_mesh, survey_lite_mesh) pass checks. No user-visible changes; API and results unchanged.
